toolsUsed: exec_command (read-only git/cat/rg/nl/sed; write owned review JSON)

evidenceClass: source audit and designed counterexamples only; no deterministic fixtures executed and no claim of gate passage

findings.title: Receipt freshness and exact execution identity
findings.counterexample: A previous passing receipt survives in a fixed path, or a receipt from another check/tree is reused while the current assertion is skipped. Merely checking IDs and JSON shape accepts stale evidence.
findings.requirement: Allocate a new absent result path per check execution; validate a fresh invocation nonce and exact check/tree identity; require a regular non-symlink file. Validate complete unique assertion IDs, strict statuses/types, and exit/result consistency. Reject missing, malformed, duplicate, cross-check, cross-tree, stale, partial, or incompatible receipts as harness evidence.
fixtures: duplicate IDs and duplicate JSON keys

findings.title: Baseline RED identifies only the declared unmet behavior
findings.counterexample: Expected assertion A fails but unrelated assertion B also fails, or a harness setup exception is converted by a broad catch into A=false. A subset-only expected-failure check still declares baseline ready.
findings.requirement: Specify exact expected baseline failure set per acceptance check, with all other declared assertions passing. Harness/setup outcomes never become assertion failure by default. The protocol cannot determine semantic intent inside a dishonestly or incorrectly authored frozen assertion; independent review must inspect the exception-to-result boundary.
fixtures: desired behavior already true with missing import
setup error plus plausible failure payload
actual intended RED and later GREEN

findings.title: Frozen execution chain covers all check kinds and allowed setup paths
findings.counterexample: Acceptance entry is frozen but delegates to a mutable runner, package.json script, pytest configuration, runtime loader, or service startup wrapper. A regression runner can likewise fabricate success. A declared chain that omits a real helper remains incomplete.
findings.requirement: Protect entry and each declared repository dependency for every check kind. Disallow unsupported setup/service/shell indirections in schema 2 or give them equivalent explicit frozen-chain declarations. Require reviewer identification of actual command/config/import chain. Document that declaration completeness and external runtime/dependency correctness are assumptions, not properties inferred by the verifier.

findings.title: Entry and chain names cannot escape the immutable snapshot
findings.counterexample: A frozen entry is a symlink to mutable external code, a ../ path escapes the tree, an absolute argv entry ignores the snapshot, or interpreter -c/-m/shell flags execute unrelated code while an evidence path is merely decorative.
findings.requirement: Define accepted argv grammar and entry position; reject command-string interpreters and unsupported alternate entry forms. Canonicalize repository paths, reject traversal/absolute paths and symlink escapes (including directory ancestors). Reject or explicitly model submodules. State external executable/runtime identity as external input.

findings.title: Resolved candidate identity stays fixed despite original checkout races
findings.counterexample: HEAD changes between capture, copying, diff computation and logging; an ignored local file affects the live run; or a concurrent edit after a cleanliness check is copied but reported as the earlier commit.
findings.requirement: Resolve candidate commit once before executing; validate input cleanliness and materialize source directly from that commit. Compute scope/protection diff between fixed base and candidate IDs. Log original resolved IDs and complete tracked-content binding, not post-run HEAD. Execute candidate checks from the isolated materialized tree; ignored inputs must be excluded unless explicitly linked and reported as external.
fixtures: original checkout changes after snapshot begins
ignored source-influencing file is not copied

findings.title: Tracked integrity checks bind original content, not only status
findings.counterexample: A check edits tracked source then commits it inside its snapshot. Post-run git status is clean, yet the executed artifact no longer matches the recorded candidate. Checking only the final tree misses mutation that affects later checks.
findings.requirement: Compare tracked paths, types/modes and bytes against the original resolved source manifest before and after each check and after setup where supported. Detect committed as well as uncommitted drift; require protected chain integrity before any later check. Explicitly distinguish observed persistent mutation detection from preventing all transient self-restoring writes, which requires a stronger execution boundary.

findings.title: Structured assertion reports are not unforgeable execution attestation
findings.counterexample: A frozen harness itself fabricates all declared statuses without performing the intended assertion, or imports mutable application code that writes the expected result. A nonce available to that process cannot establish independent execution.
findings.requirement: Phrase the guarantee as receipt completeness/freshness plus protected declared harness source. Independent evidence review must challenge fake receipts and broad exception catches. Add a documented bounded demonstration that an intentionally dishonest frozen reporter remains outside assurance; do not advertise schema 2 as proving arbitrary assertions executed.
fixtures: review a no-op reporter emitting valid statuses as a negative assurance example

findings.title: Legacy support remains visibly lower assurance in every reporting route
findings.counterexample: Schema 1 completion receives a label in JSON but --baseline or stdout still looks identical to hardened schema 2; automation treats both as the same guarantee.
findings.requirement: Give schema 1 a clear visible and recorded legacy assurance marker for baseline and candidate routes; schema 2 gets a distinct protocol marker. Preserve historical fixtures byte for byte and do not rewrite existing product contracts in place. Guidance must identify explicit migration review and fresh frozen baseline.
fixtures: legacy false-support examples retained and labeled

decision.reason: The implementation contract, schema 2 protocol and frozen grader are not yet supplied as an immutable revision. This is a design review, not a contract or implementation verdict.
decision.nextAction: Review immutable contract/protocol/grader commit supplied by parent; map each must-freeze item to assertions or explicitly bounded residual risk.
